definitions.explanation: Used after a number to count individual pieces of sushi, typically nigiri. Standard in sushi restaurants and on menus.

examples.japanese: ⟦マグロ→マグロ：11134_maguro⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧{貫|かん}⟦{注文|ちゅうもん}した→注文する：21390_chuumon⟧。
examples.english: I ordered two pieces of tuna sushi.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦セット→セット：03853_setto⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{十|じゅっ}{貫|かん}⟦{入|はい}っている→入る：00494_hairu⟧。
examples.english: This set contains ten pieces of sushi.

examples.japanese: ⟦{大将|たいしょう}→大将：19140_taishou⟧、⟦{今日|きょう}→今日：00496_kyou⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦おすすめ→おすすめ：09746_osusume⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{五|ご}→五：00697_go⟧{貫|かん}⟦{握|にぎ}って→握る：02383_nigiru⟧⟦ください→下さい：02899_kudasai⟧。
examples.english: Chef, please make me five pieces of today's recommendation.

notes:
A counter used almost exclusively in sushi contexts. Origin is debated, but it likely comes from older units of weight or coinage. A piece of nigiri sushi is sometimes (originally) two pieces served together as one {貫|かん}, but modern usage treats one piece as one {貫|かん}.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦{一|いっ}{貫|かん}→一貫：17700_ikkan_b⟧, ⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧{貫|かん}, ⟦{三|さん}→三：00749_san⟧{貫|がん}: 1, 2, 3 pieces (counting changes with sound shifts)
- ⟦{一|いち}{人前|にんまえ}→一人前：06782_ichininmae⟧{十|じゅっ}{貫|かん}: ten pieces per serving
- ⟦{握|にぎ}り{寿司|ずし}→握り寿司：19145_nigirizushi⟧⟦{二|に}→二：00736_ni⟧{貫|かん}: two pieces of nigiri sushi

USAGE:
For maki rolls (cut rolls), the counter is usually {切|き}れ or {本|ほん} (for the whole roll). {貫|かん} is reserved mainly for nigiri.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦{個|こ}→〜個：00645_ko⟧: piece (general counter) — works for sushi too in casual speech but lacks the specialist feel
- {人前|にんまえ}: portion; serving — for full sets, not individual pieces
